- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) within 5 days, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (±0.33); apply +0.5–1.5% bias to first 5–7 days.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive drops >1%), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with 1–2 day lag of true price movement.
